jobs.description:
Position Title:
Senior Director - Enterprise Performance, Evaluation and Strategic Initiatives

Employment Status:
Permanent Full Time

Position Status:
This is a Non-Bargaining Unit position

This posting is for a new vacancy.

Hours of Work:
Monday to Friday, 35 Hours

Position Reports to:
Chief Executive Officer

Salary Range: $
125,000 - $140,000, commensurate on skills and experience, plus participation in HOOPP and Group Benefits.

Primary work location:
Oshawa (Hybrid work environment); Staff may be requested to work out of other DCHC's sites in Pickering, Whitby, Ajax, Oshawa South and Oshawa North (Airport Road) as required.

Direct Reports
: 5

Manager
Quality Improvement Coordinator - 1
Health Information Specialist - 1
Data Analyst - 2

Organization

Who We Are: Durham Community Health Centre (DCHC) is a charitable registered organization that provides integrated, accessible, and equitable community-based primary care, wellness services, and health education for Durham community members facing barriers to health and well-being.

Who We Serve: DCHC offers equity-focused programs and services for priority populations, including Indigenous peoples, Black communities, 2SLGBTQI+ community members, newcomers to Canada, seniors, and clients without a family doctor. This approach helps community members access both preventive care and care when they are ill.

How We Work: Our interprofessional team includes physicians, nurse practitioners, nurses, counsellors, dietitians, outreach workers, medical secretaries, and administrative staff. Together, we place each client at the centre of care and respond to their needs through integrated clinical care, wellness support, and health education.

Why Join Now: This is an exciting time to join DCHC as we advance an energizing path toward greater impact in local health care. Guided by our Strategic Plan, Theory of Change, brand, client stories, and resources, we are diversifying, expanding, and strengthening how we serve the community.

Position Overview

Durham Community Health Center (DCHC) is seeking an exceptional, self-driven leader to take on the role of Senior Director, Enterprise Performance, Evaluation and Strategic Initiatives. The role demands a leader who thrives in complexity, excels in driving enterprise-wide performance, and is relentless in the pursuit of excellence.

At DCHC we are committed to a collaborative culture where strategic thinking, execution discipline and shared leadership are at the core of everything we do. As a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, the Senior Director will be responsible for aligning enterprise performance, strategic initiatives, and quality improvement with DCHC's long-term vision.

This role is a unique opportunity for an innovative leader to build high-impact frameworks for evaluation, decision support, special project execution and quality transformation. The right candidate will be a visionary, a doer and a collaborator; someone who can seamlessly transition between strategy and execution while fostering an organizational culture of continuous improvement and strategic excellence.

Key Responsibilities

As a member of the Executive Leadership Team and strategic advisor to the CEO, the Senior Director provides enterprise leadership across strategy execution, performance intelligence, transformation, risk, quality, accreditation, and organizational alignment.

Enterprise Strategy & Execution
Translate DCHC's strategic plan into clear annual priorities, business operating plans, performance measures, and funder accountabilities
Lead enterprise strategy execution and monitor progress against strategic commitments, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and long-term strategic objectives
Ensure alignment between Board priorities, CEO direction, ELT accountabilities, resource management, and organizational initiatives execution
Enterprise Performance & Intelligence
Establish DCHC's enterprise performance management framework
Develop integrated, real-time dashboards, scorecards, quality indicators, and performance reporting tools
Lead enterprise analytics, program evaluation, KPIs, outcome measurement, governance reporting, and data-informed decision-making
Provide the CEO and ELT with timely intelligence focusing on trends to support strategic decisions and performance improvement
Strategic Initiatives & Transformation
Lead CEO and ELT-sponsored strategic initiatives, complex enterprise projects, and transformational initiatives that improve service delivery and operational effectiveness
Establish clear governance framework, milestones, accountabilities, and measures for all organizational initiatives aligned to DCHC corporate balance scorecard
Enterprise Risk, Quality & Organizational Excellence
Lead the enterprise risk management strategy, including proactive risk identification, mitigation, monitoring, annual planning, and reporting
Lead DCHC's enterprise Quality Improvement and accreditation strategy, including organization-wide QI frameworks, and compliance reporting
Integrate quality, risk, performance, evaluation, and continuous improvement into one enterprise framework
Strengthen organizational resilience, accountability, and readiness for emerging challenges
CEO Advisory & Enterprise Alignment
Serve as a strategic advisor to the Office of the CEO
Provide executive analysis, strategic options, decision support, and recommendations that enhance program and organizational effectiveness
Lead CEO Office strategic operating plans and priority tracking
Identify and resolve cross-portfolio dependencies, competing priorities, and organizational barriers that could impede enterprise execution
Champion One DCHC, One Strategy, One Enterprise

Strategic Mandate

The Senior Director ensures DCHC has the clarity, intelligence, discipline, and execution capability to turn strategy into measurable organizational and community collective impact.

Qualifications & Experience

Education & Certifications

Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, Business Administration, or a related field (master's preferred)
PMP, Lean Six Sigma, Change Management or a relevant performance excellence certification is an asset

Experience & Skills

7-10 years of progressive senior leadership experience in enterprise performance, strategic execution, quality improvement, program evaluation, risk management, or transformation leadership
Proven success in leading high-impact initiatives, enterprise-wide projects, and complex change management efforts
Strong ability to analyze data, identify trends, and translate insights into strategic action
Deep understanding of Ontario's healthcare transformation, integrated care models, and emerging policy trends
Exceptional leadership, stakeholder engagement, and executive communication skills
Demonstrated ability to lead in a collaborative, fast-moving, and high-accountability environment

What Sets This Role Apart?

This is a high-stakes, high-impact leadership role. It requires:
A strategic powerhouse who can execute with precision
A collaborative leader who thrives in a multi-disciplinary, fast-paced environment
A change agent who is comfortable leading transformational initiatives and navigating complexity
A data-driven decision-maker who can synthesize insights into actionable strategies

Why Join DCHC?

Impact at Scale - Drive transformational change in a high-performing primary care organization
Enterprise-Level Innovation - Lead quality, performance, and strategic initiatives at the highest level
Leadership Growth - Competitive compensation, HOOPP pension, and ongoing professional development

Benefits

Comprehensive health benefits
Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan (HOOPP)
Growth and Development opportunities; annual professional development allowance

Full vaccination against COVID-19 is mandatory for this position (DCHC will however adhere to its duty to accommodate those who are unable to be fully vaccinated for a reason related to a human right protected ground).

DCHC encourages applications from individuals who reflect the diversity of the communities served, including Indigenous peoples, racialized persons, persons with disabilities, members of the 2SLGBTQIA+ community, and other equity-deserving groups.

Application Process:

While we thank all applicants for their interest in applying, only those qualified and considered for an interview will be contacted. All applicant submissions will be kept on file for six months, for future consideration
All applicants are encouraged to provide a valid email address for communication purposes. Applicants may receive written correspondence regarding this job posting directly to the email address provided on their resume. As an applicant, it is your responsibility to ensure that you check your email regularly
All positions are subject to the successful completion of the following pre-employment conditions for all external hires: Reference Checks; and Criminal Background checks (including Vulnerable Sector Screening)
Please be advised that AI Technology supports the screening process of applications. All final hiring decisions are made by our recruitment team

Interim Senior Vice President, Finance

Reports to: Chief Financial Officer

Location: Waterloo, Ontario

Duration: 6-12 Months

Hybrid

A global organization is seeking a Senior Vice President, Finance to strengthen its administrative and financial leadership capacity and support continued growth. Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, this executive will provide overall direction for finance, accounting, tax planning, credit and treasury activities worldwide.

The Senior Vice President will also provide financial support and analysis for strategic initiatives, including mergers and acquisitions, due diligence and integration, and the implementation of new technology systems and tools.

The Mandate

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Senior Vice President of Finance will:

Global Finance Leadership

Together with the CFO, contribute to the development of strategic goals and objectives by managing and developing high-performing finance teams around the world.
Provide overall direction for finance, accounting, tax, planning, credit, and treasury functions globally.
Lead the Vice President of Financial Planning & Analytics, the Vice President - Group Controller, and other members of the finance leadership team.
Act as a strategic partner to the executive team and Strategic Business Unit Managers, providing insights and decision support on commercial and operational matters.
Participate in global governance committees and contribute collaboratively to enterprise-wide decision-making.

Planning, Reporting and Performance Management

Prepare and implement financial plans aligned with the global strategy, including annual business plans and budgets that support profitable growth.
Lead the long-range plan, three-year strategic plan, annual operating plan and budget, quarterly closing, monthly reporting, and Board meeting preparation.
Prepare and present financial budgets, monthly profit and loss results, forecast-versus-budget analyses, balance sheets, and cash flow statements to the CFO, CEO, and Executive Committee.
Evaluate internal investment decisions to maximize returns and promote the efficient use of capital.
Drive value creation through operational transformation, margin expansion, improved working capital, and disciplined performance management.

Financial Control, Risk and Compliance

Ensure statutory accounts are published within agreed timelines and in accordance with applicable accounting standards.
Maintain high-quality financial reporting and effective internal controls, including compliance with IFRS and applicable financial and tax regulations.
Serve as a key contact for external auditors and manage the preparation and support required for external audits.
Set high standards for internal control, internal audit, and financial risk management, including foreign exchange exposure.
Monitor debt, maintain control of the balance sheet, and work with the CFO to manage banking facilities and relationships.

Transactions, Systems and Transformation

Work with the CFO on acquisitions, joint ventures, and partnerships, ensuring high-quality due diligence, deal execution, and integration.
Provide financial analysis and support for other strategic initiatives, including the implementation of new technology systems and tools.
Supervise the effective operation of financial systems, databases, and financial software.
Enhance and optimize financial and accounting systems, processes, tools, and control frameworks.
Lead efficiency initiatives that improve quality, reduce costs, and keep critical systems current and secure.

Leadership and Team Development

Reinforce the global finance organization and establish clear standards of accountability, collaboration, and performance.
Recruit, interview, and hire finance employees as required.
Develop culturally sensitive, high-performing teams that can operate effectively across a variety of regions and business environments .

Key Internal and External Relationships

The Senior Vice President of Finance will work closely with:
Chief Financial Officer
Chief Executive Officer and Executive Committee
Strategic Business Unit Managers
Finance leadership teams and employees globally
All levels of management and staff
Banks and external auditors
Customers, suppliers, insurance brokers, and other professional advisors

Ideal Candidate Profile

The successful candidate will bring:

15+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, ideally beginning in a large international organization recognized for strong financial processes and business performance.
Experience in a mid-sized organization is considered an asset.
Proven experience leading finance across a global scope.
A strong record of strengthening finance organizations and developing effective leadership teams.
Demonstrated value creation through operational transformation, margin expansion and disciplined execution.
Experience in life sciences, research and development, or manufacturing is an asset.
University or master’s degree with a specialization in Finance; an MBA is considered an asset.
Fluency in English is required; French-language capability is considered an asset.

Leadership Attributes

Credible and natural leadership with a positive, pragmatic, and hands-on approach.
Strong commercial judgment, analytical capability, and the ability to identify trends, issues, and opportunities.
Personal maturity, integrity, accountability, and the ability to operate effectively in a family-owned business.
A collaborative style and the ability to interact effectively with a broad range of stakeholders and cultures.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, cultural sensitivity, and multicultural openness.
A results-driven mindset with the energy and commitment to deliver meaningful improvements.

The Ideal Interim Executive

This assignment is best suited for a seasoned global finance executive who combines strategic insight with practical execution. The successful leader will be comfortable operating across planning, performance management, controllership, treasury, transactions, systems, and transformation while strengthening the global finance team.
The executive will bring credibility with senior leaders, Board-level finance processes, auditors, banks, and business partners, and will establish the disciplined processes, controls, and decision support required to advance profitable growth.

Head of Technology & AI

Reports to: Founder & CEO

Location: Remote within Canada, with travel for client and team meetings

Scope: Technology leadership across AEQ’s Financial Services and Innovate businesses

The opportunity

Aequilibrium (AEQ) is a Canadian technology company, listed among the Top 5 Digital Agencies, Fastest Growing Tech Companies, and Top Employers in British Columbia. AEQ is looking for a technology leader to help shape and drive our next stage of growth. You will be a strategic partner to the CEO and business leaders, a credible adviser to clients, and a leader who develops our technical teams.

AI is changing what clients need from professional services. We want to help them make sound choices, improve how work gets done, and bring valuable solutions into production. You will help define where AEQ should lead, build the capabilities behind that direction, and create opportunities with clients.

This is an active role with substantial client involvement. You will lead senior technology conversations, help originate and win engagements, work directly on selected client assignments, and remain accountable for the quality of the solutions we propose and deliver. You will bring particular credibility to our credit union work while helping AEQ grow in healthcare, government, and other sectors.

What you will own

Set direction and build the practice

Develop and execute AEQ’s technology and AI strategy, with a focused set of priorities, investments, and measurable outcomes
Identify emerging client needs and turn them into advisory offerings, pilots and repeatable services
Build a point of view on how AI changes software delivery and the value clients expect from a technology partner
Decide, with our business leaders, where AEQ should build expertise, form partnerships, or pursue new markets
Take ownership of progress: bring the right people together, resolve obstacles, and move priorities from discussion to delivery

Create opportunities and lead clients

Build trusted relationships with senior client leaders and help them navigate complex technology and AI decisions
Work with Sales and Delivery to develop opportunities, lead discovery, and shape proposals, architectures, estimates, and delivery plans
Serve on selected client engagements as a principal architect, strategic adviser, or fractional technology leader
Connect technology choices to business outcomes, commercial realities, implementation risk, and the client’s ability to sustain the solution
Provide technical leadership from the first client conversation through delivery, especially when an engagement changes direction or encounters a difficult decision

Make AI useful and responsible

Lead AEQ’s AI initiatives with a clear purpose, committed capacity, and a small number of valuable initiatives
Work with clients and teams to identify uses of AI with a credible path from experiment to production
Establish practical approaches to human review, privacy, security, quality and measurement
Turn successful work into capabilities AEQ can demonstrate, deliver and support, not isolated experiments

Develop our people

Coach senior technologists and help them grow as architects, client advisers and leaders
Set clear expectations for technical ownership, decision-making and collaboration across teams
Strengthen engineering and architecture practices using lessons from client delivery
Help recruit people who add technical depth, sound judgment and initiative to AEQ

What you bring

A demonstrated record of initiating, winning, and delivering technology consulting or professional services work. We will ask what you personally identified, built, and brought to a result
Deep enough technical experience to earn the trust of architects and engineers, combined with the judgment to lead business conversations
Experience advising senior clients, shaping complex proposals and making commitments that delivery teams can meet
Practical understanding of modern software architecture, cloud, integration, data and AI—including where AI is useful and where it introduces risk
Experience developing technical leaders and building capabilities that extend beyond your own contributions
Commercial understanding of a services business: scope, pricing, staffing, utilization, partnerships and client outcomes

Experience with credit unions, digital banking, or core modernization is a strong advantage. We also welcome leaders with relevant experience in healthcare, government, or other complex environments. Expertise in a particular vendor platform is not required.

How you will work at AEQ

You will report to the CEO and partner closely with the leaders of Financial Services sales, Delivery, and Innovate. You will lead our technology direction while giving senior technologists meaningful ownership in their areas of expertise.

We expect approximately half your time to involve clients and pursuits as the practice develops, including paid advisory work, solution leadership and strategic presales. We will set billable and commercial targets separately so the time required to build the practice is clear.

What success looks like after six months

AEQ has a focused technology and AI plan that the leadership team and technical leads are actively executing
You have helped originate or advance meaningful client opportunities, with clear evidence of your contribution
Major pursuits and engagements have credible technical leadership, sound estimates, and clear delivery ownership
The AI pod has demonstrated a valuable capability and has a defined route to a client pilot or production use
Clients seek AEQ’s advice on consequential technology decisions, and our technical leads have grown through your coaching and trust

Why join AEQ

AEQ is at a point where a technology leader can shape what we become. You will work directly with our founder and business leaders, influence which opportunities we pursue, and help turn promising ideas into services clients use. Our work spans credit unions, healthcare, government and immersive technology, giving you room to build an AI practice with real client problems, experienced technologists and a clear path from strategy to delivery.

Compensation

This full-time executive role offers a base salary of CAD $160,000–$200,000
, plus a performance bonus tied to agreed business growth, client, and leadership outcomes. The successful candidate will also be eligible for consideration for stock option grants under AEQ’s executive stock option plan, subject to the plan terms and grant approval. The package includes benefits and support for professional development.
